hypothesis: Giving every harness invocation a tool-runtime session identity distinct from its trace span, routing that identity through every KOTA-owned tool loop, and applying inherited provider-egress filtering after all execution overlays merge will isolate approved credentials across concurrent workflow items, projects, and interactive sessions without weakening approval or injection-defense boundaries.

metricsCompared.name: cross-session credential isolation
metricsCompared.baseline: get_secret assigned the approved value to daemon process.env, so later execution environments for unrelated sessions and projects inherited it.
metricsCompared.candidate: Focused regressions prove process.env stays unchanged and only the exact live scopeId plus sessionId overlay receives the credential; unrelated and ended sessions receive no value.

metricsCompared.name: harness credential lifetime
metricsCompared.baseline: Harness runs had no credential-overlay lifecycle, so daemon-global values could survive successful and failed runs.
metricsCompared.candidate: The neutral harness wrapper assigns a unique tool-runtime session per invocation and erases it after successful and throwing adapters. Persistent Telegram conversations own an outer reference until clear, project switch, or shutdown, and long-lived subprocess resources terminate with that owner.

metricsCompared.name: concurrent agent execution isolation
metricsCompared.baseline: Concurrent foreach agents for the same run and step reused one workflow span as their credential-map key.
metricsCompared.candidate: A concurrent same-span regression proves each harness invocation receives a distinct session id and can observe only its own credential value.

metricsCompared.name: eval provider credential boundary
metricsCompared.baseline: Execution filtering ran before caller and session overlays, allowing get_secret or context.env to restore provider auth and proxy values.
metricsCompared.candidate: The inherited provider-egress boundary is captured before merging and enforced afterward; a regression proves both session and caller overlays cannot restore filtered auth, proxy, or policy variables.

metricsCompared.name: approval and risk posture
metricsCompared.baseline: get_secret was moderate risk and queued in supervised mode before daemon-global injection.
metricsCompared.candidate: get_secret remains moderate risk and supervised-queued, while approved execution fails closed when the originating scoped session is no longer live.

rationale: This is a fail-closed repair to a confirmed high-severity credential boundary. The candidate preserves approval and risk classification, removes daemon process.env mutation, keys overlays by canonical scope plus a runtime session identity that is not a reusable trace span, and requires that identity to be live. KOTA-routable adapters receive the same typed context; persistent Telegram sessions own explicit teardown; final execution filtering prevents provider auth or proxy restoration after overlay merge. REPLs and background groups remain bound to session teardown. Focused tests cover cross-session, cross-project, stale approval, concurrent same-span agents, persistent channel lifecycle, provider-egress bypass attempts, and successful or exceptional cleanup.
